findings.evidence: The three files contain `@[expose] public section`; `ChainComplex.lean` already provides `normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_X`, `_obj_d_apply`, and `_map_f_apply`, while `Excision.lean` exposes `cubicalHomologyδ` despite its public exactness and comparison lemmas.
findings.fix: Remove these section-wide `@[expose]` attributes and add targeted characterization lemmas for any projections or reductions genuinely needed across module boundaries.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes every definition body in this file; the same over-exposure occurs in `Comparison/Models.lean:38` and `Comparison/Excision.lean:39`.

findings.evidence: `Relative.lean:231` defines only `singularCubicalHomologyIso_hom`; the parallel absolute API has both `_hom` at `HomotopyInvariance.lean:76` and `_inv` at line 83, and `cubicalToSingularRel` is public at `Relative.lean:149`.
findings.fix: Add a `[simp]` theorem characterizing `(singularCubicalHomologyIso k P n).inv`, preferably as `HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cubicalToSingularRel k P) n`, with the necessary homology-level inverse proof.
findings.issue: The relative `singularCubicalHomologyIso` characterizes only `.hom`, leaving users unable to rewrite `.inv` to the advertised reverse comparison map without unfolding or reproving that relationship.

summary: The public surface exposes implementation bodies unnecessarily and leaves the relative comparison isomorphism without an elimination rule for its inverse.
